Auxiliary input interlock is open. 1. Check remote wiring. 2. Verify communications programming for intentional fault.

FRN 5.03 and earlier only. The DC bus voltage fell below under voltage level within 200 ms of a start command, DC bus ripple voltage in excess excessive, or an input phase loss has been detected. 1. Monitor the incoming AC line for low voltage or line power interruption. 2. Check input fuses.
DC bus voltage fell below the minimum value. 1. Monitor the incoming AC line for low voltage or line power interruption. 2. Check input fuses.

DC bus voltage exceeded the maximum value. Monitor the AC line for high line voltage or transient conditions. Bus overvoltage can also be caused by motor regeneration. Extend the decel time or install a dynamic brake chopper.
Drive unable to accelerate motor. Increase P039 - A147 (Accel Time x) or reduce load so drive output current does not exceed the current set by parameter A179.

Internal electronic overload trip. 1. An excessive motor load exists. Reduce load so drive output current does not exceed the current set by parameter P033 (Motor OL Current). 2. Verify A170 (Boost Select) setting.

Heatsink temperature exceeds a predefined value. 1. Check for blocked or dirty heatsink fins. Verify that ambient temperature has not exceeded 45°C (113°F) for IP30/NEMA 1/UL Type 1 installations or 50°C (122°F) for IP20/Open type installations. 2. Check fans.

The drive output current has exceeded the hardware current limit. Check programming. Check for excess load, improper A170 (Boost Select) setting, DC brake volts set too high or other causes of excess current.
A current path to earth ground has been detected at one or more of the the drive output terminals. Check the motor and external wiring to the drive output terminals for a grounded condition.
Output current has dropped below the level set in A184 (Load Loss Level). Check for load loss.

FRN 6.xx and later. Excessive DC bus ripple voltage detected. See d329 (DC Bus Ripple V). Check incoming power for a missing phase or blown fuse. If drive is used intentionally with single phase input, apply output derating of 35% actual drive rating.
An analog input is configured to fault on signal loss. A signal loss has occurred. Configure with T072 (Analog In Loss). 1. Check parameters. 2. Check for broken or loose connections at inputs.
FRN 6.xx and later. A loss of fan feedback has been detected. (Frames E and F only). Make sure cooling fans are clear of debris and spinning freely. Replace fan if necessary.
Drive unsuccessfully attempted to reset a fault and resume running for the programmed number of A163 (Auto Rstrt Tries). Correct cause of the fault and manually clear.

The communication network has faulted. 1. Cycle power. 2. Check communications cabling. 3. Check network adapter setting. 4. Check external network status.

Increase C106 (Comm Loss Time) to an appropriate time for application. 4. Change C105 (Comm Loss Action) to a value other than 0 (fault) if appropriate for the application.

The checksum read from the board does not match the checksum calculated. Set P041 (Reset To Defaults) to option 1 (Reset Defaults).
Failure has been detected in the drive control and I/O section. 1. Cycle power. 2. Replace drive if fault cannot be cleared.
Failure of temp probe T1 (dew point). Check cabling or replace probe if bad.

Main contactor checkback: If a main contactor checkback is configured, no checkback occurs within the time set in P600 after the power-up command. In the case of externally excited synchronous motors (P095 = 12), there is no checkback for the excitation current unit.

Pre-charging: When pre-charging, the minimum DC link voltage (P071 Line Volts x 1.34) of 80 % has not been reached.
The maximum pre-charging time of 3 seconds has been exceeded.
DC link overvoltage: Shutdown has occurred due to excessive DC link voltage.

DC link undervoltage: The lower limit value of 76 % of the DC link voltage (P071 Line Volts), or of 61 % when kinetic buffering has been enabled, has been fallen short of.
Undervoltage in the DC link in ’normal’ operation (i.e. no SIMULATION).
Undervoltage in the DC link with active kinetic buffering and speed less than 10 % of the rated motor speed.
It was a ’brief power failure’ which was not detected until system recovery (auto restart flag).
DC link overvoltage: Due to excessive DC link voltage, shutdown has taken place.

Overcurrent: Overcurrent shutdown has occurred.
The shutdown threshold has been exceeded.
I too low: During excitation of the induction motor, the current did not rise above 12.5 % of the setpoint magnetizing current for no-load operation.
I too low: During excitation of the motor, the current component is less than 25 % of the motor no- load current.
Motor stall: Motor has stalled or is locked.
SAFE STOP: SAFE STOP operating or failure of the 24 V power supply during operation.
F set fly: The found set frequency could not be implemented.
Motor not found: During flying restart without tachometer: Search in both directions of rotation not possible (one direction blocked) and motor has not been found.
Motor temperature: The motor temperature limit value has been exceeded.
Motor I2t: Parameterized limit value of the I2t monitoring for the motor has been exceeded.
Inverter temperature: The limit value of the inverter temperature has been exceeded.
UCE Ph. L1: UCE upper switch (Compact PLUS) / or UCE has tripped in phase L1.
UCE Ph. L2: UCE lower switch (Compact PLUS) / or UCE has tripped in phase L2.
UCE Ph. L3: Fault pulse resistor (Compact PLUS) / or UCE has tripped in phase L3
Supply phase: The frequency and the amplitude of the DC link ripple indicate a single-phase power failure.
Meas. value sensing: A fault has occurred in the measured value sensing system.
Ext. Fault 1: Parameterizable external fault input 1 has been activated.
Ext. Fault 2: Parameterizable external fault input 2 has been activated.
Analog input: An analog input is taking place in operating mode 4..20mA and a wire break has occurred.
Voltage OFF during parameter storage: During a parameter task, a voltage failure has occurred on the board.
EEPROM fault: A fault has occurred when storing the values in the EEPROM.
BICO manager fault: A fault has occurred during the softwiring of binectors and connectors.
Opt. Board: A hardware fault has occurred when accessing an optional board.
Par. Task: A fault has occurred during the transfer of parameters to the gating unit processor.
Gating Calc Time: The calculating time in the gating unit computer is not sufficient.
Gating Pulse Freq: The pulse frequency set in P340 is not permissible.
SW version: The firmware versions on the CU have different firmware release.
TSY Init.: Error when initializing the TSY board.
Speed encoder: Digital tachometer or analog tachometer sensing are faulty.

n-Cntr.Input: Control track input (-X103/27, or -X104/27 Compact PLUS) is not high:
- Tachometer line broken
- Tachometer fault
The fault input on the TSY was activated.
Tachometer dn/dt: The permissible change value of the speed encoder signal P215 dn(act,perm) has been doubly exceeded.
Sensor board initialization fault: A fault has occurred during initialization of the encoder board.
SIMOLINK telegram failure: Communication on the SIMOLINK ring is disturbed.
Brake does not open: The brake has not opened, the output current of the converter has exceeded the parameterized current threshold (U840) for longer than one second (with the rotor locked)
Parameter fault Parameter task: A fault has occurred during the processing of a parameter task.
Parameter fault after factory setting/init.: A fault has occurred in the initialization phase during the calculation of a parameter.
MLFB is missing: This is set if the MLFB = 0 after exiting INITIALIZATION (0.0 kW). MLFB = order number.

Incorrect parameterization: A parameter entered during drive setting (e.g. P107 Mot Rtd Freq, P108 Mot Rtd Speed,
Incorrect P340 Pulse Frequency) is not in a permissible parameterization range (depending on control type)
Multi-parallel circuit not Compact PLUS: Fault in connection with the multi-parallel circuit or board ImP1 has been detected.
Scom Telegram: No telegram was received at an Scom interface (Scom/USS protocol) within the telegram failure time.
SCB initialization fault not Compact PLUS: A fault has occurred during initialization of the SCB board.
EB initialization fault: A fault has occurred during initialization of the EB board.
AnInp1SL1: 4 mA at analog input 1, slave 1 fallen short of
AnInp2 SL1: 4 mA at analog input 2, slave 1 fallen short of
AnInp3 SL1: 4 mA at analog input 3, slave 1 fallen short of
AnInp1 SL2: 4 mA at analog input 1, slave 2 fallen short of
AnInp2 SL2: 4 mA at analog input 2, slave 2 fallen short of
AnInp3 SL2: 4 mA at analog input 3, slave 2 fallen short of
SCB telegram failure: No telegram has been received by the SCB (USS, peer-to-peer, SCI) within the telegram failure time.
TB/CB initialization fault: Fault during initialization of the board at the DPR interface
OptBrdHeartbeat-Counter: Heartbeat-counter of the optional board is no longer being processed
TB/CB telegram failure: No new process data have been received by the TB or the CB within the telegram failure time
Add. CB initialization fault: A fault has occurred during initialization of the CB board.
SIMOLINK initialization fault: A fault has occurred during initialization of the SLB board.
Mld Param.: An error occurred when attempting to change a parameter from the standstill measurement or the rotating measurement (Mot ID).

Mld Time: The rotating measurement takes longer than programmed in a measured status. Possible causes:
Load torque too high
Load torque not uniform Ramp-function generator disabled

Mld n(set): Due to entries for
- Permissible phase sequence
- Maximum frequency,
- Minimum speed,
- Changeover frequency between V and I model,
- Start of field-weakening frequency,
- Frequency suppression bandwidth
it was not possible to determine a permissible frequency range for the rotating measurement.
Mld abort: The rotating measurement was aborted due to the inadmissible external intervention.

Mld meausred value: The measured values for the nominal ramp-up time when optimizing the controller deviate too greatly.
Cause: very unsteady load torque

Mld Tachof: The rotating measurement has detected a fault in the speed actual value signal. The fault value defines the type of fault.
The fault measurement may have been erroneously generated if the drive speed is externally forced (e.g. completely locked drive generates the "no signal" message)
GRND Init: During the ground fault test, a current not equal to zero has been measured, or an UCE or overcurrent monitoring has responded, although no value has yet been triggered.
GRND UCE: During the ground fault test, the UCE monitoring has responded in a phase in which no valve has been triggered.
GRND Phase: During the ground fault test, a current flows in a phase in which no valve has been triggered or the UCE monitoring has responded in the phase in which the valve has been triggered.

Ground fault: There is a ground fault or a fault in the power section.
During the ground fault test, a current flows from the phase in which a valve has been triggered, the overcurrent comparator has responded, or a UCE monitoring has responded in a phase in which a valve has been triggered.
MLd = 0: A fault has occurred during the test pulse measurement

Mld Unsym: During the DC measurement, the measurement results for the individual phases differ significantly. The fault value indicates which quantity(ies) is (are) concerned and in which phase the greatest deviation occurred.
Mld R(L): The rotor resistance determined during DC measurement deviates too significantly from the value which was calculated by the automatic parameterization from the rated slip.

Mld di/dt: During test pulse measurement, the current has increased significantly faster than was expected. Thus for the 1st test pulse, an overcurrent condition occurred within the first half of the minimum switch-on time
Fault e_Func: A fault has occurred while calculating the equalization function.
Unsym I_sigma: The individual leakage test results deviate too significantly.

MId OFF: The converter has automatically stopped the automatic measurement due to the time limit up to power-up having been exceeded or due to an OFF command during the measurement, and has reset the function selection in P115.
KF internal: A fault has occurred during calculations in the context of the MotID.
Technology board fault: See TB documentation
Fault 1 Function blocks: An active signal is present at binector U061
Fault 2 Function blocks: An active signal is present at binector U062
Fault 3 Function blocks: An active signal is present at binector U063
Fault 4 Function blocks: An active signal is present at binector U064
Signs of life repeatedly invalid.: After an appropriate number of invalid signs of life, the sign of life monitoring block has gone into fault status.
Link int.: Fault in internal linking. One of the two linked partners does not reply.
ParaLink int.: Fault in the internal parameter linking.
Fault in EEPROM: A fault has occurred in the EEPROM.
Time slot overflow: A time slot overflow which cannot be corrected has been detected in the higher-priority time slots.
Access fault Optional board: Serious faults have occurred while making access to external optional boards (CB, TB, SCB, TSY ..).
RAM: A fault has occurred during the test of the RAM.
EPROM fault: A fault has occurred during the test of the EPROM.
Invalid processor command should be processed.
Invalid format in a protected processor command.
Wrong firmware version: A version conflict between the firmware and the hardware has occurred.

FF processing: Unexpected fatal error
(During processing of the fatal errors, a fault number has occurred which is unknown to date).
